previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after experiencing syncope in the waiting room of a clinic, preceded by lightheadedness and no food or fluid intake that morning. Initial evaluation revealed hypotension, metabolic acidosis, and elevated lactate, with no evidence of cardiac ischemia on serial troponins or EKG changes. A CT chest ruled out pulmonary embolism but incidentally showed new mild C7 and T2 vertebral compression fractures, deemed chronic and asymptomatic. She was treated with IV fluids, leading to stabilization of vital signs and resolution of symptoms. Fluconazole was discontinued due to QT prolongation risk. She remained stable on telemetry, with no arrhythmias, and was discharged home with instructions to increase oral hydration and follow up with her oncologist and primary care providers.
